subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should OpenClaw status treat live gateway memory runtime health as the source of truth for memory-plugin availability, or is the current `not checked`/embedding-readiness split the intended behavior?
rationale: The current code partly avoids the old false negative, but the remaining behavior is a product/API contract choice and an open linked PR proposes a narrower live-gateway-provider interpretation.

options.title: Adopt live-runtime health semantics
options.body: Review and either land or replace the linked live-gateway memory-provider PR so status can show plugin runtime health independently of embedding readiness.

options.title: Keep status inconclusive by design
options.body: Close the linked PR and document that status avoids memory-runtime health claims unless explicit memory diagnostics are run.

options.title: Move the remainder to the broader issue
options.body: Use `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599` as the single tracker for live-gateway versus CLI-local memory status behavior and close duplicates only after that scope is captured.

recommendation.title: Adopt live-runtime health semantics
recommendation.body: Review and either land or replace the linked live-gateway memory-provider PR so status can show plugin runtime health independently of embedding readiness.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across the gateway doctor and memory-runtime code paths that define this behavior.
